## Rule

Colors 1, 2, and 4 are vertically aligned to color 1. Let `top(c)` be the
first row containing color `c` inside the active 10-column grid. Color 1 stays
fixed; colors 2 and 4 are shifted by `top(1) - top(c)` rows, preserving columns
and shape. Channel 0 is background inside the active input height (5 or 10 rows)
where no shifted nonzero color lands; padding outside that height is all-zero.
Channels 3 and 5-9 are zero.

## Algorithm sketch

Verified on `corpus.build(30, want=200000)`:

```python
out = zeros_like(input)
h = input_height  # corpus has only 5 or 10, width always 10
target = min(row for row, col in cells(input, 1))
for color in (1, 2, 4):
    src_top = min(row for row, col in cells(input, color))
    dr = target - src_top
    for r, c in cells(input, color):
        out[r + dr, c] = color
out[:h, :10][out[:h, :10] == 0] = 0  # encoded as ch0=1 in ONNX
```

Best ONNX (`task030_v20_hprobe_slice9`) uses a negative-pad Conv to emit 10-row
UINT16 column bit-codes for colors 1/2/4, gets top rows via
`Cast(UINT16->BOOL) -> Cast(UINT8) -> ArgMax`, splits the three top scalars,
shifts colors 2/4 with INT8 row-index plumbing and U16 row `Gather`, builds
channel-0 background with U16 OR/XOR against the active-row mask, pads the
compact channel/row table to 30 rows with a reused 10-row zero tail, and makes a
final `BitwiseAnd(row_bits, col_bits)` the free graph output. v20 replaces the
old 10-param height probe Conv with an 8-param `Slice` of row9/ch0, because h=10
always has background at row9/col0 while h=5 is padding there.

## Cost analysis

Current LIVE cost is 14,534 (memory 14,382 + params 152), already crop-to-10x10
and `Sum`-folded. Its remaining cost is dominated by F32 10x10 channel planes,
F32 shifted masks, a full 10-channel crop, and a F32 output assembly.

`task030_v20_hprobe_slice9` costs 1,882 (memory 1,415 + params 467). Main charged
tensors: `row_ch30 [1,10,30,1]` U16 = 600 B; `row_ch10 [1,10,10,1]` U16 = 200
B; the Conv row-code output and U16 cast = 180 B; row-index/top/height plumbing
is the rest. The final `[1,10,30,30]` `BitwiseAnd` output is free.

The price of dropping the 900 B single-channel padded label canvas is a higher
param bill: `row_weight [3,10,1,10]` = 300 params and the static U16 zero row
tail = 100 params reused twice. This still wins because the final row/column
bitset decoder removes the seven 10x10 U8 planes and padded label canvas from
v4.

Final-op enumeration: `ScatterND` is wrong for this dense vertical-shift output;
BOOL Concat+Pad works (4,050) but pays a 1,000 B `[1,10,10,10]` intermediate;
U8 canvas + final Equal wins by using a 900 B single-channel padded label canvas;
bit-packed U8 plus final Equal is better still. Broadcast-Add/BitwiseAnd tails
do not naturally express arbitrary shifted source masks plus active-height ch0.

Sub-1000 pressure: v20 already removed the 900 B label canvas, but the strict
10-channel raw-output contract still carries the 600 B U16 row table, 200 B U16
active table, 300-param row-code Conv, and background/height plumbing. The
rejected 1,816 score-output rung is cheap but invalid because the harness uses
raw `(output > 0)` rather than argmax.

2026-06-07 re-price against Onnx_Advanced #68/#78/#79:

- PLACER-CONV/QLinearConv (#78): current final `BitwiseAnd(row_bits, col_bits)`
  is already a free output node. A placer Conv only wins if the pre-output tensor
  is already a spatial channel grid. From v20 row bitsets, materializing decoded
  `[1,10,10,10]` costs at least 1000 B as BOOL/U8, or 2000 B via U16
  `BitwiseAnd`, before Conv weights. A 1x1 Conv/QLinearConv cannot turn scalar
  labels `{0,1,2,4,pad}` into singleton one-hot equality classes; it is affine
  per channel. Kill: `>=1000 B + 100 params` decoded-grid tail, worse than the
  current 600 B row table plus 200 B active table. QLinearConv has the same
  equality problem and adds mandatory quant inputs; `y_zp` being U8 does not
  create arbitrary class tests.
- #68 contraction discriminator: the vertical shifts are separable per axis, but
  the selected offset and ch0 complement are not free. A final contraction over
  cropped 10x10 input first pays a F32 `[1,10,10,10]` crop = 4000 B. A selected
  row-matrix bank for two shifted colors is at least `2*30*10 = 600` selector
  cells before column/channel/background terms; full 30x30 selectors are 2700+
  cells. Params-only row banks over 15 offsets cost `15*30*10 = 4500` params per
  shifted color if emitting 30 rows. Kill: separability passes, but every
  contraction route pays selector matrices or dense banks larger than v20's
  467 params and does not remove enough of the 1415 B memory.
- #79 LUT crossover: current computed route is 1882. Shift-index
  parameter-LUT route needs two `[15,10]` INT8 banks = 300 params; it saves only
  the `src_i8/safe_i8` arithmetic chain, roughly 18-38 B per two colors after
  still paying gathered indices/casts. Net is about +250 B worse. Output-LUT or
  decoded-grid routes are the measured v2/v4/v12 family (3849/2479/2315) or
  `>=1000 B` for a decoded 10-channel active grid before tail. Full row-tuple
  LUT has 218 observed row tuples, so `218*10` row-mask params before class
  generation. Kill: computed U16 row-bitset remains the crossover winner.
- i32 BitwiseAnd class-LUT (#78/task345): nonzero color row masks have 31 classes,
  but background has 38 and the 10-channel row tuple has 218. A U8 class-id row
  table `[1,10,30,1]` = 300 B cannot answer "class contains output column c" in
  one final op; it needs dynamic `1<<class` or a class-to-bitset gather, which
  recreates an i32/U16 row-bitset plane (`[1,10,30,1]` i32 = 1200 B, U16 = 600
  B). Kill: task345's static class-bitmask trick does not map cleanly because
  Task030's dynamic object is the row mask itself, not a small output-column
  class.
- Boundary trap: v20 adopts no positive off-center free-output Conv. Existing
  negative-pad Conv is the row-code entry, not the output placer; the row9/ch0
  probe is a plain `Slice`. If a later placer Conv uses off-center positive taps,
  run the FREE-OUTPUT BOUNDARY LEAK battery before any floor claim.

## Don't-do log

- Do not use the `1 - ch0` foreground shortcut; row 5 padding detection must sum
  all channels at a cell because row-5 cells are sometimes nonzero in 10-row cases.
- Do not drop channel 0 or emit only nonzero colors. Byte-equality requires ch0=1
  for background cells inside active rows and all-zero outside the active height.
- Do not use `ScatterND` for this dense output; a label canvas plus free final
  `Equal` is cheaper than sparse channel patching.
- Do not treat the 5-row and 10-row cases as visible-only. The 200k corpus split
  is 100,100 height-5 and 99,900 height-10, so active-height gating is required.
- `Sum(UINT8)` is not an ORT kernel here; `task030_v4` uses variadic `Max(UINT8)`
  instead. This is valid because a 200k corpus check found zero overlaps among
  the shifted color 1/2/4 bitplanes.
- The min-only gather shortcut is corpus-verified: negative row indices wrap into
  zero rows, while positive OOB indices are clamped to row 9. Full truth and A/B
  passed after this trim.
- Do not submit the `convscore5`/argmax-score idea as-is. Even at cost 1,816,
  the local visible gate is 0/266 because outputs are multi-hot after `>0` and
  have only five channels.
- The official `run_network` contract is raw `(output > 0).astype(float)`, not
  argmax or score-normalization. Candidate outputs must be canonical 10-channel
  one-hot masks, including channel 0 background.
- Row9/ch0 is a safe 5-vs-10 height probe for the current corpus: h=10 always
  has background there, and h=5 is padding. Do not use rows5-8/ch0 as a simple
  probe; row5/col0 is nonzero in 18,722 h=10 corpus cases.
- The no-active-gate shifted-row shortcut is verified in v10/v11/v14: shifted U16
  color rows remain byte-equal on visible plus full 200k truth/A-B.
- Negative begin-padding in the v11/v14 height-probe Conv
  (`pads=[-5,0,-24,-29]`)
  is locally accepted by checker/ORT/scorer and passed full 200k gates.
- Sparse initializers are not currently submit-safe. Raw ORT can run them, and
  sanitizer-stable `safe_name_N` sparse names can make visible pass, but the
  official scorer calls ONNX `check_model(..., full_check=True)`/shape inference;
  sparse Conv weights fail there with `unsupported type: sparse_tensor(float)`.
- Compact LUT routes are gated by index width. `Gather` accepts INT32/INT64
  indices here, so a 10-channel compact decoder pays about 1,200 B just for an
  INT32 index plane before it can beat the row-bitset tail.
- `task030_v12_pack64` proves UINT64 bitwise/shift kernels run locally, but the
  packed row-word decoder scored 2,315, worse than v14.
- `ArgMax(BOOL)` is not an ORT kernel; the BOOL->UINT8 hop before ArgMax is
  mandatory.
- `Where(BOOL, U16, U16)` is not an ORT kernel; keep the U16 active mask as
  `Cast(active_rows) * fullmask`.
- PLACER Conv/QLinearConv is not a win unless the graph already has a decoded
  spatial channel grid. Scalar labels cannot be equality-decoded by a 1x1 affine
  Conv, and decoded 10-channel active grids cost at least 1000 B before tail
  params.
- Do not replace computed row shifts with `[15,10]` parameter-LUT banks unless a
  later scorer changes index costs. Two banks add 300 params and save only about
  18-38 B of row-index memory.
- Do not claim contraction final is dead because shifts are nonseparable; they
  are separable. It is dead here because selected offset matrices/background
  complement cost more than the current U16 row-bitset final.
- The 31-class observation applies only to nonzero color row masks. Background
  masks have 38 classes and full 10-channel row tuples have 218, so the task345
  i32 class-LUT pattern does not replace the row-bitset table directly.
